Senior Developer Engineer focused on code fixes TASK — PR REWORK. You are the rework agent for ONE pull request. The ticket folder input/ (PR diff, pr_discussions.md review threads, CI failures) IS your task: (1) answer EVERY open review thread in outputs/review_replies.json, (2) apply the code/test fixes on this PR's branch following TDD, (3) push. Never ask what to fix — the input folder defines it. Success = every thread has a targeted reply and the fixed code is pushed (when the threads require code changes). ## agent_task_preamble.md You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ## coding_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Coding Guidelines — follow existing codebase patterns and conventions"] G2["Before implementing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists in project root or subdirectories → READ and FOLLOW it — it contains agent-specific instructions, coding styles, and conventions"] G4["If skills are available in the project → USE them — they provide specialized capabilities, workflows, and tool integrations"] G5["Instructions may be extended via project configuration — always follow the full set of provided instructions"] G6["Never invent new patterns when the codebase already has an established way of doing things"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 --> G5 --> G6 ``` ## general_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD START([Ticket enters rework]) --> SETUP{rework_setup_failed.md exists?} SETUP -->|Yes| FAIL[Write setup failure response and stop] SETUP -->|No| INPUT[Read ALL input files in the ticket subfolder] INPUT --> INPUTS["request.md, comments.md, existing_questions.json, parent_context_*.md, pr_info.md, pr_diff.txt, merge_conflicts.md, ci_failures.md, ci_failures_full.log, review_state.md, pr_discussions.md, pr_discussions_raw.json"] INPUTS --> CONFLICTS{merge_conflicts.md exists?} CONFLICTS -->|Yes| RESOLVE["Resolve every conflict marker, git add each file, verify with git diff --check"] CONFLICTS -->|No| CI RESOLVE --> CI{ci_failures.md or ci_failures_full.log exists?} CI -->|Yes| OWNED{"Violations you must fix (N owned) table at the top?"} OWNED -->|Yes| FIX_OWNED["Fix EVERY owned violation (path:line, rule, measured vs limit)
— an owned violation may NOT be dismissed as unrelated/
not caused by this PR/infra; dispute per item with disputed: <reason> only
when the gate itself is wrong"] OWNED -->|No| FIX_CI["Fix CI root cause: dependencies, config, or test setup"] FIX_OWNED --> THREADS FIX_CI --> THREADS[Address every open thread in pr_discussions.md] THREADS --> BLOCKING{BLOCKING issues?} BLOCKING -->|Yes| FIX_BLOCK["Fix BLOCKING first — security, critical bugs"] FIX_BLOCK --> IMPORTANT BLOCKING -->|No| IMPORTANT[Fix IMPORTANT issues] IMPORTANT --> SUGGESTIONS{Minor suggestions?} SUGGESTIONS -->|Yes| SKIP["Skip if time-consuming — note in response.md"] SUGGESTIONS -->|No| TEST["Follow TDD approach for every fix — see tdd_approach.md — then run tests and verify"] SKIP --> TEST TEST --> OUTPUT[Write outputs/response.md] OUTPUT --> REPLIES{Open review threads?} REPLIES -->|Yes| REVIEW_REPLIES["Write outputs/review_replies.json with one reply per open thread using threadId + inReplyToId"] REPLIES -->|No| END([End]) REVIEW_REPLIES --> END ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/review_state.md — reviewer verdict + decision state (CHANGES_REQUESTED = blocking)"] P7["7️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 --> P7 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify the rework addresses all ACs. ## 2. Owned CI violations — no dismissal `ci_failures.md` opens with machine-extracted violation tables: - **"Violations you must fix (N owned)"** — each row (`check`, `rule`, `path:line`, measured-vs-limit) is in a file changed by this PR's diff. Owned = blocking. Fix it, or dispute it **per item** with `disputed: ` when the gate itself is wrong. - **"Foreign / infra reds (do not chase)"** — reds in files this PR does not touch. Do not fix them here; mention them in the summary. The full uncapped list lives in `ci_violations.json`. In `outputs/response.md`, **list every owned violation with `fixed` or `disputed: `**. A summary that claims the reds are "not caused by this PR" / "unrelated" / "infra" while owned violations are open is mechanically rejected: the leg fails and the no-op loop guard counts the lap. For `dart_format` owned items (rule `dart_format` — the `static` job failed on `dart format --set-exit-if-changed`), the expected fix is `dart format .` on the whole tree, then verify with `dart format --set-exit-if-changed --output=none .` before pushing. ## 3. Already-addressed / invalid threads (gh-957 audit-resolve) The thread list in `pr_discussions.md` / `pr_discussions_raw.json` comes from the SAME GraphQL reviewThreads census the SM armer counts (gh-957) — if it lists threads, they are really open on GitHub and each one needs exactly one reply entry in `outputs/review_replies.json`. A reply entry does NOT always imply a code commit: - **Already addressed** — verify against the current head; cite the commit/file/line that covers the finding. - **Invalid finding** — explain precisely why it does not apply to this code. When every open thread has a targeted reply and the pass pushed no commits, the post-action resolves the threads with an explanatory audit line (rework run URL) per thread — this is the ONLY permitted resolution-without-changes path. Partial coverage resolves NOTHING: the pass is reported blocked. Never leave an open thread without a reply entry. ## tdd_approach.md ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph TDD["TDD for PR Rework — RED-GREEN-REFACTOR"] T0["Start from the concrete issue: a CI failure, a review thread, or a BLOCKING/IMPORTANT finding"] T1["RED: Write or extend a test that REPRODUCES the reported issue
— must fail before the fix
— cover the exact scenario called out (including boundary/multi-item cases, not just the happy path)"] T2["GREEN: Make the minimum code change to turn the test PASS
— do not expand scope beyond the reported issue"] T3["REFACTOR: Clean up while keeping tests GREEN
— run the full test suite after every change"] T4{"More findings to address?"} T5["Repeat RED-GREEN-REFACTOR for the next finding"] T0 --> T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 T4 -->|Yes| T5 --> T1 …

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1751
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1751
- **Title**: gh-1744 [BUG] Lossy decodeSessionCwd replaces hyphens with slashes breaking mailbox wake for dashed folder names
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1744` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 7
- **Additions**: +301
- **Deletions**: -25
- **Created**: 2026-10-21T16:48:09Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-21T17:29:55Z

## PR Description

Closes #1744
### Root Cause

`_encodeCwd` flattens `/`, `\`, `:` into `-` and `decodeSessionCwd` reverses that with `split('-').join('/')` — a many-to-one mapping. A literal `-` in a directory name is indistinguishable from an encoded separator, so any hyphenated workspace (e.g. `/Users/Yury_Bakhmutski/_w/postal-nl`) decodes to a path that does not exist (`.../postal/nl`). `MailboxEntry.cwd` and `messages-registry.json` carry the bogus path, and the mailbox-wake spawn dies with `ProcessException: No such file or directory` — an asleep mailbox can never be woken.

### Fix

- `lib/src/session/session_repo.dart`: slug encoding is reversible now — `%`→`%25`, literal `-`→`%2D`, `:`→`%3A` escape before separators flatten, so hyphens round-trip exactly. Paths without those characters encode byte-identically to the legacy scheme (existing on-disk slug folders and pi's layout stay stable). `decodeSessionCwd` unescapes per segment when a slug carries escapes, keeping the legacy split for legacy slugs.
- `lib/src/messaging/file_messaging_repository.dart`: `_recordRegistry` stores the live env's exact cwd instead of a lossy slug round-trip; `directory()` prefers the registry's exact cwd (keyed by mailbox `.id`), falling back to slug decode. Registry read extracted into `_readRegistry()`.
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_inbox.dart`: wake spawning extracted into public `launchMailboxWake` — verifies the cwd exists (and is not a plain file) before spawning and returns a named refusal instead of a raw process exception; `AgentCli._launchMailboxWake` delegates to it.

### Test Coverage

- Reproduction tests (RED before, PASSED after): hyphenated-cwd slug round-trip + reversible-slug layout (`session_repo_test.dart`); exact-cwd registry write + registry-preferred `directory()` (`file_messaging_repository_test.dart`); wake refusal for missing/file cwd without spawning (`agent_cli_test.dart`).
- Full suite `dart test --exclude-tags integration`: **11572 passed, 0 failed**, 11 skipped (pre-existing env-gated: qjs, sandbox-exec, FA_IMPORT_E2E machine gates).

### Notes

- Legacy on-disk slugs of hyphenated projects stay ambiguous (unchanged decode); the registry-preferred cwd repairs their wake path. New sessions write reversible slugs.
- No breaking changes: hyphen-free cwds produce byte-identical slugs; session listing reads cwd from file headers, not slugs.

`file_messaging_repository.dart:382`:

`registry?[id]` is `dynamic`. ```

|---|---|---|
| `--tmp-a%2Db--` | `/tmp/a%2Db` | `/tmp/a-b` |
| `--tmp-a%2Fb--` | `/tmp/a%2Fb` | `/tmp/a/b` |
| `--tmp-a%25b--` | `/tmp/a%25b` | `/tmp/a%b` (lossy) |

The PR notes only acknowledge the hyphen ambiguity ("Legacy on-disk slugs of hyphenated projects stay ambiguous (unchanged decode)"); this class is not mentioned. Impact is bounded — the decode only feeds the `directory()` fallback now that the registry's exact cwd is preferred, and a wrong fallback cwd is refused by name in `launchMailboxWake` instead of crashing — so this is documentation, not behavior, work: extend the `decodeSessionCwd` doc comment (and ideally the PR notes) to name the `%2D`/`%2F`/`%5C`/`%3A`/`%25` legacy-text flip.

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-21):

`session_repo.dart:122` — `:` now escapes to `%3A`, so any cwd containing a colon encodes to a **different on-disk slug folder** than the legacy scheme. # gh-1744: [BUG] Lossy decodeSessionCwd replaces hyphens with slashes breaking mailbox wake for dashed folder names

## Description

## Problem Summary
`decodeSessionCwd` irreversibly turns hyphens in directory names into path separators:
- `lib/src/session/session_repo.dart:109`: `_encodeCwd` replaces `/`, `\`, `:` with `-`.
- `lib/src/session/session_repo.dart:123`: `decodeSessionCwd` does `inner.split('-').join('/')`.

### Impact
For any workspace containing hyphens (e.g., `/Users/Yury_Bakhmutski/_w/postal-nl`), `decodeSessionCwd` decodes it as:
`/Users/Yury_Bakhmutski/_w/postal/nl` (which does not exist!).

Consumers of `decodeSessionCwd`:
1. `file_messaging_repository.dart:373` (`directory()`): populates `MailboxEntry.cwd` with the bogus path.
2. `file_messaging_repository.dart:444` (`_recordRegistry`): persists the non-existent path into `messages-registry.json`.
3. `subagent_tools.dart:624` & `agent_cli.dart:1106` (`_launchMailboxWake`): attempts `Process.start` with `workingDirectory: entry.cwd`, resulting in:
   `ProcessException: No such file or directory`

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1751
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1751
- **Title**: gh-1744 [BUG] Lossy decodeSessionCwd replaces hyphens with slashes breaking mailbox wake for dashed folder names
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1744` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 7
- **Additions**: +301
- **Deletions**: -25
- **Created**: 2026-10-21T16:48:09Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-21T17:29:55Z

## PR Description

Closes #1744
### Root Cause

`_encodeCwd` flattens `/`, `\`, `:` into `-` and `decodeSessionCwd` reverses that with `split('-').join('/')` — a many-to-one mapping. A literal `-` in a directory name is indistinguishable from an encoded separator, so any hyphenated workspace (e.g. `/Users/Yury_Bakhmutski/_w/postal-nl`) decodes to a path that does not exist (`.../postal/nl`). `MailboxEntry.cwd` and `messages-registry.json` carry the bogus path, and the mailbox-wake spawn dies with `ProcessException: No such file or directory` — an asleep mailbox can never be woken.

### Fix

- `lib/src/session/session_repo.dart`: slug encoding is reversible now — `%`→`%25`, literal `-`→`%2D`, `:`→`%3A` escape before separators flatten, so hyphens round-trip exactly. Paths without those characters encode byte-identically to the legacy scheme (existing on-disk slug folders and pi's layout stay stable). `decodeSessionCwd` unescapes per segment when a slug carries escapes, keeping the legacy split for legacy slugs.
- `lib/src/messaging/file_messaging_repository.dart`: `_recordRegistry` stores the live env's exact cwd instead of a lossy slug round-trip; `directory()` prefers the registry's exact cwd (keyed by mailbox `.id`), falling back to slug decode. Registry read extracted into `_readRegistry()`.
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_inbox.dart`: wake spawning extracted into public `launchMailboxWake` — verifies the cwd exists (and is not a plain file) before spawning and returns a named refusal instead of a raw process exception; `AgentCli._launchMailboxWake` delegates to it.

### Test Coverage

- Reproduction tests (RED before, PASSED after): hyphenated-cwd slug round-trip + reversible-slug layout (`session_repo_test.dart`); exact-cwd registry write + registry-preferred `directory()` (`file_messaging_repository_test.dart`); wake refusal for missing/file cwd without spawning (`agent_cli_test.dart`).
- Full suite `dart test --exclude-tags integration`: **11572 passed, 0 failed**, 11 skipped (pre-existing env-gated: qjs, sandbox-exec, FA_IMPORT_E2E machine gates).

### Notes

- Legacy on-disk slugs of hyphenated projects stay ambiguous (unchanged decode); the registry-preferred cwd repairs their wake path. New sessions write reversible slugs.
- No breaking changes: hyphen-free cwds produce byte-identical slugs; session listing reads cwd from file headers, not slugs.

`file_messaging_repository.dart:382`:

```dart
final registryCwd = registry?[id]?['cwd'];
```

`registry?[id]` is `dynamic`. final registryCwd = entry is Map<String, dynamic> ? entry['cwd'] : null;
```dart
final cwd = (registryCwd is String && registryCwd.isNotEmpty)

    : _decodeSessionCwd?.call(slugDir.name);
```

| `--tmp-a%2Db--` | `/tmp/a%2Db` | `/tmp/a-b` |
| `--tmp-a%2Fb--` | `/tmp/a%2Fb` | `/tmp/a/b` |
| `--tmp-a%25b--` | `/tmp/a%25b` | `/tmp/a%b` (lossy) |

The PR notes only acknowledge the hyphen ambiguity ("Legacy on-disk slugs of hyphenated projects stay ambiguous (unchanged decode)"); this class is not mentioned. **ai-teammate** (2026-10-21):

`session_repo.dart:122` — `:` now escapes to `%3A`, so any cwd containing a colon encodes to a **different on-disk slug folder** than the legacy scheme. # gh-1744: [BUG] Lossy decodeSessionCwd replaces hyphens with slashes breaking mailbox wake for dashed folder names

## Description

## Problem Summary
`decodeSessionCwd` irreversibly turns hyphens in directory names into path separators:
- `lib/src/session/session_repo.dart:109`: `_encodeCwd` replaces `/`, `\`, `:` with `-`.
- `lib/src/session/session_repo.dart:123`: `decodeSessionCwd` does `inner.split('-').join('/')`.

### Impact
For any workspace containing hyphens (e.g., `/Users/Yury_Bakhmutski/_w/postal-nl`), `decodeSessionCwd` decodes it as:
`/Users/Yury_Bakhmutski/_w/postal/nl` (which does not exist!).

Consumers of `decodeSessionCwd`:
1. `file_messaging_repository.dart:373` (`directory()`): populates `MailboxEntry.cwd` with the bogus path.
2. `file_messaging_repository.dart:444` (`_recordRegistry`): persists the non-existent path into `messages-registry.json`.
3. `subagent_tools.dart:624` & `agent_cli.dart:1106` (`_launchMailboxWake`): attempts `Process.start` with `workingDirectory: entry.cwd`, resulting in:
   `ProcessException: No such file or directory`
   The asleep mailbox can never be woken up by incoming agent mail.

## Proposed Fix
1. Encode slug reversibly (e.g. percent-encoding or escaping hyphens as `--`).
2. Have `directory()` and `_launchMailboxWake` prefer the exact verified `cwd` stored in `messages-registry.json` or verify `Directory(cwd).existsSync()` before attempting process spawn.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1751
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1751
- **Title**: gh-1744 [BUG] Lossy decodeSessionCwd replaces hyphens with slashes breaking mailbox wake for dashed folder names
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1744` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 7
- **Additions**: +301
- **Deletions**: -25
- **Created**: 2026-10-21T16:48:09Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-21T17:29:55Z

## PR Description

Closes #1744
### Root Cause

`_encodeCwd` flattens `/`, `\`, `:` into `-` and `decodeSessionCwd` reverses that with `split('-').join('/')` — a many-to-one mapping. A literal `-` in a directory name is indistinguishable from an encoded separator, so any hyphenated workspace (e.g. `/Users/Yury_Bakhmutski/_w/postal-nl`) decodes to a path that does not exist (`.../postal/nl`). `MailboxEntry.cwd` and `messages-registry.json` carry the bogus path, and the mailbox-wake spawn dies with `ProcessException: No such file or directory` — an asleep mailbox can never be woken.

### Fix

- `lib/src/session/session_repo.dart`: slug encoding is reversible now — `%`→`%25`, literal `-`→`%2D`, `:`→`%3A` escape before separators flatten, so hyphens round-trip exactly. Paths without those characters encode byte-identically to the legacy scheme (existing on-disk slug folders and pi's layout stay stable). `decodeSessionCwd` unescapes per segment when a slug carries escapes, keeping the legacy split for legacy slugs.
- `lib/src/messaging/file_messaging_repository.dart`: `_recordRegistry` stores the live env's exact cwd instead of a lossy slug round-trip; `directory()` prefers the registry's exact cwd (keyed by mailbox `.id`), falling back to slug decode. Registry read extracted into `_readRegistry()`.
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_inbox.dart`: wake spawning extracted into public `launchMailboxWake` — verifies the cwd exists (and is not a plain file) before spawning and returns a named refusal instead of a raw process exception; `AgentCli._launchMailboxWake` delegates to it.

### Test Coverage

- Reproduction tests (RED before, PASSED after): hyphenated-cwd slug round-trip + reversible-slug layout (`session_repo_test.dart`); exact-cwd registry write + registry-preferred `directory()` (`file_messaging_repository_test.dart`); wake refusal for missing/file cwd without spawning (`agent_cli_test.dart`).
- Full suite `dart test --exclude-tags integration`: **11572 passed, 0 failed**, 11 skipped (pre-existing env-gated: qjs, sandbox-exec, FA_IMPORT_E2E machine gates).

### Notes

- Legacy on-disk slugs of hyphenated projects stay ambiguous (unchanged decode); the registry-preferred cwd repairs their wake path. New sessions write reversible slugs.
- No breaking changes: hyphen-free cwds produce byte-identical slugs; session listing reads cwd from file headers, not slugs.

`file_messaging_repository.dart:382`:

```dart

```

`registry?[id]` is `dynamic`. If `~/.fah/messages-registry.json` is valid JSON but an entry is not an object (e.g. `{"sess1/main": "corrupted by another tool"}`), `?['cwd']` dispatches `operator []` with a `String` argument on a non-Map → uncaught `NoSuchMethodError`, and **`directory()` throws** — taking down `agent_directory` and wake-target resolution with it. `FormatException` is caught in `_readRegistry`, but this is a *shape* error, not a parse error, so it escapes.

```dart
final registryCwd = entry is Map<String, dynamic> ? entry['cwd'] : null;
```


|---|---|---|

| `--tmp-a%2Fb--` | `/tmp/a%2Fb` | `/tmp/a/b` |
| `--tmp-a%25b--` | `/tmp/a%25b` | `/tmp/a%b` (lossy) |

The PR notes only acknowledge the hyphen ambiguity ("Legacy on-disk slugs of hyphenated projects stay ambiguous (unchanged decode)"); this class is not mentioned. **ai-teammate** (2026-10-21):

`session_repo.dart:122` — `:` now escapes to `%3A`, so any cwd containing a colon encodes to a **different on-disk slug folder** than the legacy scheme. # gh-1744: [BUG] Lossy decodeSessionCwd replaces hyphens with slashes breaking mailbox wake for dashed folder names

## Description

## Problem Summary
`decodeSessionCwd` irreversibly turns hyphens in directory names into path separators:
- `lib/src/session/session_repo.dart:109`: `_encodeCwd` replaces `/`, `\`, `:` with `-`.
- `lib/src/session/session_repo.dart:123`: `decodeSessionCwd` does `inner.split('-').join('/')`.

### Impact
For any workspace containing hyphens (e.g., `/Users/Yury_Bakhmutski/_w/postal-nl`), `decodeSessionCwd` decodes it as:
`/Users/Yury_Bakhmutski/_w/postal/nl` (which does not exist!).

Consumers of `decodeSessionCwd`:
1. `file_messaging_repository.dart:373` (`directory()`): populates `MailboxEntry.cwd` with the bogus path.
2. `file_messaging_repository.dart:444` (`_recordRegistry`): persists the non-existent path into `messages-registry.json`.
3. `subagent_tools.dart:624` & `agent_cli.dart:1106` (`_launchMailboxWake`): attempts `Process.start` with `workingDirectory: entry.cwd`, resulting in:
   `ProcessException: No such file or directory`
   The asleep mailbox can never be woken up by incoming agent mail.

## Proposed Fix
1. Encode slug reversibly (e.g. percent-encoding or escaping hyphens as `--`).
2. Have `directory()` and `_launchMailboxWake` prefer the exact verified `cwd` stored in `messages-registry.json` or verify `Directory(cwd).existsSync()` before attempting process spawn.

## Machine jobs

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1751
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1751
- **Title**: gh-1744 [BUG] Lossy decodeSessionCwd replaces hyphens with slashes breaking mailbox wake for dashed folder names
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1744` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 7
- **Additions**: +301
- **Deletions**: -25
- **Created**: 2026-10-21T16:48:09Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-21T17:29:55Z

## PR Description

Closes #1744
### Root Cause

`_encodeCwd` flattens `/`, `\`, `:` into `-` and `decodeSessionCwd` reverses that with `split('-').join('/')` — a many-to-one mapping. A literal `-` in a directory name is indistinguishable from an encoded separator, so any hyphenated workspace (e.g. `/Users/Yury_Bakhmutski/_w/postal-nl`) decodes to a path that does not exist (`.../postal/nl`). `MailboxEntry.cwd` and `messages-registry.json` carry the bogus path, and the mailbox-wake spawn dies with `ProcessException: No such file or directory` — an asleep mailbox can never be woken.

### Fix

- `lib/src/session/session_repo.dart`: slug encoding is reversible now — `%`→`%25`, literal `-`→`%2D`, `:`→`%3A` escape before separators flatten, so hyphens round-trip exactly. Paths without those characters encode byte-identically to the legacy scheme (existing on-disk slug folders and pi's layout stay stable). `decodeSessionCwd` unescapes per segment when a slug carries escapes, keeping the legacy split for legacy slugs.
- `lib/src/messaging/file_messaging_repository.dart`: `_recordRegistry` stores the live env's exact cwd instead of a lossy slug round-trip; `directory()` prefers the registry's exact cwd (keyed by mailbox `.id`), falling back to slug decode. Registry read extracted into `_readRegistry()`.
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_inbox.dart`: wake spawning extracted into public `launchMailboxWake` — verifies the cwd exists (and is not a plain file) before spawning and returns a named refusal instead of a raw process exception; `AgentCli._launchMailboxWake` delegates to it.

### Test Coverage

- Reproduction tests (RED before, PASSED after): hyphenated-cwd slug round-trip + reversible-slug layout (`session_repo_test.dart`); exact-cwd registry write + registry-preferred `directory()` (`file_messaging_repository_test.dart`); wake refusal for missing/file cwd without spawning (`agent_cli_test.dart`).
- Full suite `dart test --exclude-tags integration`: **11572 passed, 0 failed**, 11 skipped (pre-existing env-gated: qjs, sandbox-exec, FA_IMPORT_E2E machine gates).

### Notes

- Legacy on-disk slugs of hyphenated projects stay ambiguous (unchanged decode); the registry-preferred cwd repairs their wake path. New sessions write reversible slugs.
- No breaking changes: hyphen-free cwds produce byte-identical slugs; session listing reads cwd from file headers, not slugs.

# gh-1744: [BUG] Lossy decodeSessionCwd replaces hyphens with slashes breaking mailbox wake for dashed folder names

## Description

## Problem Summary
`decodeSessionCwd` irreversibly turns hyphens in directory names into path separators:
- `lib/src/session/session_repo.dart:109`: `_encodeCwd` replaces `/`, `\`, `:` with `-`.
- `lib/src/session/session_repo.dart:123`: `decodeSessionCwd` does `inner.split('-').join('/')`.

### Impact
For any workspace containing hyphens (e.g., `/Users/Yury_Bakhmutski/_w/postal-nl`), `decodeSessionCwd` decodes it as:
`/Users/Yury_Bakhmutski/_w/postal/nl` (which does not exist!).

Consumers of `decodeSessionCwd`:
1. `file_messaging_repository.dart:373` (`directory()`): populates `MailboxEntry.cwd` with the bogus path.
2. `file_messaging_repository.dart:444` (`_recordRegistry`): persists the non-existent path into `messages-registry.json`.
3. `subagent_tools.dart:624` & `agent_cli.dart:1106` (`_launchMailboxWake`): attempts `Process.start` with `workingDirectory: entry.cwd`, resulting in:
   `ProcessException: No such file or directory`
   The asleep mailbox can never be woken up by incoming agent mail.

## Proposed Fix
1. Encode slug reversibly (e.g. percent-encoding or escaping hyphens as `--`).
2. Have `directory()` and `_launchMailboxWake` prefer the exact verified `cwd` stored in `messages-registry.json` or verify `Directory(cwd).existsSync()` before attempting process spawn.

## Machine jobs

    "description": "## Problem Summary
`decodeSessionCwd` irreversibly turns hyphens in directory names into path separators:
- `lib/src/session/session_repo.dart:109`: `_encodeCwd` replaces `/`, `\`, `:` with `-`.
- `lib/src/session/session_repo.dart:123`: `decodeSessionCwd` does `inner.split('-').join('/')`.

### Impact
For any workspace containing hyphens (e.g., `/Users/Yury_Bakhmutski/_w/postal-nl`), `decodeSessionCwd` decodes it as:
`/Users/Yury_Bakhmutski/_w/postal/nl` (which does not exist!).

Consumers of `decodeSessionCwd`:
1. `file_messaging_repository.dart:373` (`directory()`): populates `MailboxEntry.cwd` with the bogus path.
2. `file_messaging_repository.dart:444` (`_recordRegistry`): persists the non-existent path into `messages-registry.json`.
3. `subagent_tools.dart:624` & `agent_cli.dart:1106` (`_launchMailboxWake`): attempts `Process.start` with `workingDirectory: entry.cwd`, resulting in:
   `ProcessException: No such file or directory`
   The asleep mailbox can never be woken up by incoming agent mail.

## Proposed Fix
1. Encode slug reversibly (e.g. percent-encoding or escaping hyphens as `--`).
2. Have `directory()` and `_launchMailboxWake` prefer the exact verified `cwd` stored in `messages-registry.json` or verify `Directory(cwd).existsSync()` before attempting process spawn.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1751
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1751
- **Title**: gh-1744 [BUG] Lossy decodeSessionCwd replaces hyphens with slashes breaking mailbox wake for dashed folder names
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1744` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 7
- **Additions**: +301
- **Deletions**: -25
- **Created**: 2026-10-21T16:48:09Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-21T17:29:55Z

## PR Description

Closes #1744
### Root Cause

`_encodeCwd` flattens `/`, `\`, `:` into `-` and `decodeSessionCwd` reverses that with `split('-').join('/')` — a many-to-one mapping. A literal `-` in a directory name is indistinguishable from an encoded separator, so any hyphenated workspace (e.g. `/Users/Yury_Bakhmutski/_w/postal-nl`) decodes to a path that does not exist (`.../postal/nl`). `MailboxEntry.cwd` and `messages-registry.json` carry the bogus path, and the mailbox-wake spawn dies with `ProcessException: No such file or directory` — an asleep mailbox can never be woken.

### Fix

- `lib/src/session/session_repo.dart`: slug encoding is reversible now — `%`→`%25`, literal `-`→`%2D`, `:`→`%3A` escape before separators flatten, so hyphens round-trip exactly. Paths without those characters encode byte-identically to the legacy scheme (existing on-disk slug folders and pi's layout stay stable). `decodeSessionCwd` unescapes per segment when a slug carries escapes, keeping the legacy split for legacy slugs.
- `lib/src/messaging/file_messaging_repository.dart`: `_recordRegistry` stores the live env's exact cwd instead of a lossy slug round-trip; `directory()` prefers the registry's exact cwd (keyed by mailbox `.id`), falling back to slug decode. Registry read extracted into `_readRegistry()`.
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_inbox.dart`: wake spawning extracted into public `launchMailboxWake` — verifies the cwd exists (and is not a plain file) before spawning and returns a named refusal instead of a raw process exception; `AgentCli._launchMailboxWake` delegates to it.

### Test Coverage

- Reproduction tests (RED before, PASSED after): hyphenated-cwd slug round-trip + reversible-slug layout (`session_repo_test.dart`); exact-cwd registry write + registry-preferred `directory()` (`file_messaging_repository_test.dart`); wake refusal for missing/file cwd without spawning (`agent_cli_test.dart`).
- Full suite `dart test --exclude-tags integration`: **11572 passed, 0 failed**, 11 skipped (pre-existing env-gated: qjs, sandbox-exec, FA_IMPORT_E2E machine gates).

### Notes

# gh-1744: [BUG] Lossy decodeSessionCwd replaces hyphens with slashes breaking mailbox wake for dashed folder names

## Description

## Problem Summary
`decodeSessionCwd` irreversibly turns hyphens in directory names into path separators:
- `lib/src/session/session_repo.dart:109`: `_encodeCwd` replaces `/`, `\`, `:` with `-`.
- `lib/src/session/session_repo.dart:123`: `decodeSessionCwd` does `inner.split('-').join('/')`.

### Impact
For any workspace containing hyphens (e.g., `/Users/Yury_Bakhmutski/_w/postal-nl`), `decodeSessionCwd` decodes it as:
`/Users/Yury_Bakhmutski/_w/postal/nl` (which does not exist!).

Consumers of `decodeSessionCwd`:
1. `file_messaging_repository.dart:373` (`directory()`): populates `MailboxEntry.cwd` with the bogus path.
2. `file_messaging_repository.dart:444` (`_recordRegistry`): persists the non-existent path into `messages-registry.json`.
3. `subagent_tools.dart:624` & `agent_cli.dart:1106` (`_launchMailboxWake`): attempts `Process.start` with `workingDirectory: entry.cwd`, resulting in:
   `ProcessException: No such file or directory`
   The asleep mailbox can never be woken up by incoming agent mail.

## Proposed Fix
1. Encode slug reversibly (e.g. percent-encoding or escaping hyphens as `--`).
2. Have `directory()` and `_launchMailboxWake` prefer the exact verified `cwd` stored in `messages-registry.json` or verify `Directory(cwd).existsSync()` before attempting process spawn.

## Machine jobs
- [x] ▶ dev (fa-bug-dev) · [run](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/39633416208) · started 16:18 · done 16:48 ✅

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1751
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1751
- **Title**: gh-1744 [BUG] Lossy decodeSessionCwd replaces hyphens with slashes breaking mailbox wake for dashed folder names
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1744` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 7
- **Additions**: +301
- **Deletions**: -25
- **Created**: 2026-10-21T16:48:09Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-21T17:29:55Z

## PR Description

Closes #1744
### Root Cause

`_encodeCwd` flattens `/`, `\`, `:` into `-` and `decodeSessionCwd` reverses that with `split('-').join('/')` — a many-to-one mapping. A literal `-` in a directory name is indistinguishable from an encoded separator, so any hyphenated workspace (e.g. `/Users/Yury_Bakhmutski/_w/postal-nl`) decodes to a path that does not exist (`.../postal/nl`). `MailboxEntry.cwd` and `messages-registry.json` carry the bogus path, and the mailbox-wake spawn dies with `ProcessException: No such file or directory` — an asleep mailbox can never be woken.

### Fix

- `lib/src/session/session_repo.dart`: slug encoding is reversible now — `%`→`%25`, literal `-`→`%2D`, `:`→`%3A` escape before separators flatten, so hyphens round-trip exactly. Paths without those characters encode byte-identically to the legacy scheme (existing on-disk slug folders and pi's layout stay stable). `decodeSessionCwd` unescapes per segment when a slug carries escapes, keeping the legacy split for legacy slugs.
- `lib/src/messaging/file_messaging_repository.dart`: `_recordRegistry` stores the live env's exact cwd instead of a lossy slug round-trip; `directory()` prefers the registry's exact cwd (keyed by mailbox `.id`), falling back to slug decode. Registry read extracted into `_readRegistry()`.
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_inbox.dart`: wake spawning extracted into public `launchMailboxWake` — verifies the cwd exists (and is not a plain file) before spawning and returns a named refusal instead of a raw process exception; `AgentCli._launchMailboxWake` delegates to it.

### Test Coverage

- Reproduction tests (RED before, PASSED after): hyphenated-cwd slug round-trip + reversible-slug layout (`session_repo_test.dart`); exact-cwd registry write + registry-preferred `directory()` (`file_messaging_repository_test.dart`); wake refusal for missing/file cwd without spawning (`agent_cli_test.dart`).
- Full suite `dart test --exclude-tags integration`: **11572 passed, 0 failed**, 11 skipped (pre-existing env-gated: qjs, sandbox-exec, FA_IMPORT_E2E machine gates).

### Notes

- Legacy on-disk slugs of hyphenated projects stay ambiguous (unchanged decode); the registry-preferred cwd repairs their wake path. New sessions write reversible slugs.
- No breaking changes: hyphen-free cwds produce byte-identical slugs; session listing reads cwd from file headers, not slugs.

`file_messaging_repository.dart:382`:

`registry?[id]` is `dynamic`. If `~/.fah/messages-registry.json` is valid JSON but an entry is not an object (e.g. `{"sess1/main": "corrupted by another tool"}`), `?['cwd']` dispatches `operator []` with a `String` argument on a non-Map → uncaught `NoSuchMethodError`, and **`directory()` throws** — taking down `agent_directory` and wake-target resolution with it. `FormatException` is caught in `_readRegistry`, but this is a *shape* error, not a parse error, so it escapes.

The sibling method two functions above guards exactly this shape — please mirror it:

```dart

final registryCwd = entry is Map<String, dynamic> ? entry['cwd'] : null;
final cwd = (registryCwd is String && registryCwd.isNotEmpty)
```

|---|---|---|
| `--tmp-a%2Db--` | `/tmp/a%2Db` | `/tmp/a-b` |
| `--tmp-a%2Fb--` | `/tmp/a%2Fb` | `/tmp/a/b` |
| `--tmp-a%25b--` | `/tmp/a%25b` | `/tmp/a%b` (lossy) |

The PR notes only acknowledge the hyphen ambiguity ("Legacy on-disk slugs of hyphenated projects stay ambiguous (unchanged decode)"); this class is not mentioned. Impact is bounded — the decode only feeds the `directory()` fallback now that the registry's exact cwd is preferred, and a wrong fallback cwd is refused by name in `launchMailboxWake` instead of crashing — so this is documentation, not behavior, work: extend the `decodeSessionCwd` doc comment (and ideally the PR notes) to name the `%2D`/`%2F`/`%5C`/`%3A`/`%25` legacy-text flip.

### Thread 5 — `lib/src/session/session_repo.dart` line 122

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-21):
💡 **SUGGESTION: call out the Windows/colon slug churn in the PR notes**

`session_repo.dart:122` — `:` now escapes to `%3A`, so any cwd containing a colon encodes to a **different on-disk slug folder** than the legacy scheme. Unlike hyphens (which occur in maybe some workspace names), a colon is in **every Windows drive-letter path** (`C:\Users\...` → legacy `--C-Users-…--`, new `--C%3A-Users-…--`). This is the same accepted coexistence trade-off the ticket documents for hyphens, so no code change is requested — one sentence in the PR notes ("every Windows path changes slug; old slug folders coexist") would keep the migration story honest for the Windows hosts this repo builds (`build-windows` legs).

# gh-1744: [BUG] Lossy decodeSessionCwd replaces hyphens with slashes breaking mailbox wake for dashed folder names

## Description

## Problem Summary
`decodeSessionCwd` irreversibly turns hyphens in directory names into path separators:
- `lib/src/session/session_repo.dart:109`: `_encodeCwd` replaces `/`, `\`, `:` with `-`.
- `lib/src/session/session_repo.dart:123`: `decodeSessionCwd` does `inner.split('-').join('/')`.

### Impact
For any workspace containing hyphens (e.g., `/Users/Yury_Bakhmutski/_w/postal-nl`), `decodeSessionCwd` decodes it as:
`/Users/Yury_Bakhmutski/_w/postal/nl` (which does not exist!).

Consumers of `decodeSessionCwd`:
1. `file_messaging_repository.dart:373` (`directory()`): populates `MailboxEntry.cwd` with the bogus path.
2. `file_messaging_repository.dart:444` (`_recordRegistry`): persists the non-existent path into `messages-registry.json`.
3. `subagent_tools.dart:624` & `agent_cli.dart:1106` (`_launchMailboxWake`): attempts `Process.start` with `workingDirectory: entry.cwd`, resulting in:
   `ProcessException: No such file or directory`
   The asleep mailbox can never be woken up by incoming agent mail.

## Proposed Fix
1. Encode slug reversibly (e.g. percent-encoding or escaping hyphens as `--`).
2. Have `directory()` and `_launchMailboxWake` prefer the exact verified `cwd` stored in `messages-registry.json` or verify `Directory(cwd).existsSync()` before attempting process spawn.

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-21):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: registry entry shape is unguarded in `directory()` — a non-map entry crashes the whole listing**

`file_messaging_repository.dart:382`:

```dart
final registryCwd = registry?[id]?['cwd'];
```

`registry?[id]` is `dynamic`. If `~/.fah/messages-registry.json` is valid JSON but an entry is not an object (e.g. `{"sess1/main": "corrupted by another tool"}`), `?['cwd']` dispatches `operator []` with a `String` argument on a non-Map → uncaught `NoSuchMethodError`, and **`directory()` throws** — taking down `agent_directory` and wake-target resolution with it. `FormatException` is caught in `_readRegistry`, but this is a *shape* error, not a parse error, so it escapes.

The sibling method two functions above guards exactly this shape — please mirror it:

```dart
final entry = registry?[id];
final registryCwd = entry is Map<String, dynamic> ? entry['cwd'] : null;
final cwd = (registryCwd is String && registryCwd.isNotEmpty)
    ? registryCwd
    : _decodeSessionCwd?.call(slugDir.name);
```

A regression test with a non-map registry entry (no spawn needed, `MemoryExecutionEnv` suffices) would pin it.

```dart
if (info.isErr || (kind != FileKind.directory && kind != FileKind.symlink)) {
```

2. `FileKind` is documented as pi's semantics: *"Symlinks are not followed automatically."* On any backend honoring that (lstat), **symlink→file** would pass this check and then die with the raw `ProcessException: No such file or directory` — the exact failure mode gh-1744 exists to prevent.

Neither blocks the merge (current hosts behave correctly), but the doc comment's "`Directory(cwd).existsSync()` semantics … symlinks stay allowed" overstates the guarantee. Consider resolving the link (`fileInfo` on the target) or scoping the comment, and note why the arm exists — there is currently no test exercising it (the memory env cannot produce `symlink`).

| `--tmp-a%2Fb--` | `/tmp/a%2Fb` | `/tmp/a/b` |
| `--tmp-a%25b--` | `/tmp/a%25b` | `/tmp/a%b` (lossy) |

The PR notes only acknowledge the hyphen ambiguity ("Legacy on-disk slugs of hyphenated projects stay ambiguous (unchanged decode)"); this class is not mentioned. Impact is bounded — the decode only feeds the `directory()` fallback now that the registry's exact cwd is preferred, and a wrong fallback cwd is refused by name in `launchMailboxWake` instead of crashing — so this is documentation, not behavior, work: extend the `decodeSessionCwd` doc comment (and ideally the PR notes) to name the `%2D`/`%2F`/`%5C`/`%3A`/`%25` legacy-text flip.

### Thread 5 — `lib/src/session/session_repo.dart` line 122

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-21):
💡 **SUGGESTION: call out the Windows/colon slug churn in the PR notes**

`session_repo.dart:122` — `:` now escapes to `%3A`, so any cwd containing a colon encodes to a **different on-disk slug folder** than the legacy scheme. Unlike hyphens (which occur in maybe some workspace names), a colon is in **every Windows drive-letter path** (`C:\Users\...` → legacy `--C-Users-…--`, new `--C%3A-Users-…--`). # gh-1744: [BUG] Lossy decodeSessionCwd replaces hyphens with slashes breaking mailbox wake for dashed folder names

## Description

## Problem Summary
`decodeSessionCwd` irreversibly turns hyphens in directory names into path separators:
- `lib/src/session/session_repo.dart:109`: `_encodeCwd` replaces `/`, `\`, `:` with `-`.
- `lib/src/session/session_repo.dart:123`: `decodeSessionCwd` does `inner.split('-').join('/')`.

### Impact
For any workspace containing hyphens (e.g., `/Users/Yury_Bakhmutski/_w/postal-nl`), `decodeSessionCwd` decodes it as:
`/Users/Yury_Bakhmutski/_w/postal/nl` (which does not exist!).

Consumers of `decodeSessionCwd`:
1. `file_messaging_repository.dart:373` (`directory()`): populates `MailboxEntry.cwd` with the bogus path.
2. `file_messaging_repository.dart:444` (`_recordRegistry`): persists the non-existent path into `messages-registry.json`.
3. `subagent_tools.dart:624` & `agent_cli.dart:1106` (`_launchMailboxWake`): attempts `Process.start` with `workingDirectory: entry.cwd`, resulting in:
   `ProcessException: No such file or directory`
   The asleep mailbox can never be woken up by incoming agent mail.

## Proposed Fix
1. Encode slug reversibly (e.g. percent-encoding or escaping hyphens as `--`).
2. Have `directory()` and `_launchMailboxWake` prefer the exact verified `cwd` stored in `messages-registry.json` or verify `Directory(cwd).existsSync()` before attempting process spawn.

## Machine jobs
- [x] ▶ dev (fa-bug-dev) · [run](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/39633416208) · started 16:18 · done 16:48 ✅

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1751._

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `test/cli/agent_cli_test.dart` line 2713

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-21):
🚨 **BLOCKING: CI red — `test/cli/agent_cli_test.dart` is over the 2800-line god-file ceiling**

Both failed checks on commit `da5c4175` trace to one root cause introduced by this PR:

- **CRAP + duplication** leg: `[FAIL] loc: 1/943 files over their limit — test/cli/agent_cli_test.dart: 2861 lines > max 2800` (`crap4dart check --config crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml --only loc`, exit 2)
- **Quality gate** (aggregate): `Quality gate FAILED: a leg is failure (guards)` — the `guards` leg *is* the "CRAP + duplication" job (`ci.yml:1672-1673`), so the aggregate is red because of the same LOC violation.

`AGENTS.md` is explicit: *"Max 2800 lines per `.dart` file (crap4dart `loc` gate, issue #1234 …)"* and *"God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere … when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files"*.

The file sat at 2798 lines on `main` (2 lines under the ceiling); this PR's +63 lines push it to 2861.

**Fix options** (either satisfies the gate):
1. Move the new `group('launchMailboxWake')` and its `_RecordingShell` helper into a new test file (e.g. `test/cli/agent_cli_inbox_wake_test.dart`). The group only uses public API (`launchMailboxWake`, `MemoryExecutionEnv`, `ShellExecResult`), so no `part`/privacy gymnastics are needed.
2. Split `agent_cli_test.dart` by concern into `part` files, per the established repo pattern (`agent_cli_inbox.dart` exists exactly for this reason).

Please re-run the gates after the move — everything else in this PR is green (`static`, `test-core`, `coverage-gate`, `flutter-analyze` all pass).

---

### Thread 2 — `lib/src/messaging/file_messaging_repository.dart` line 382

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-21):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: registry entry shape is unguarded in `directory()` — a non-map entry crashes the whole listing**

`file_messaging_repository.dart:382`:

```dart
final registryCwd = registry?[id]?['cwd'];
```

`registry?[id]` is `dynamic`. If `~/.fah/messages-registry.json` is valid JSON but an entry is not an object (e.g. `{"sess1/main": "corrupted by another tool"}`), `?['cwd']` dispatches `operator []` with a `String` argument on a non-Map → uncaught `NoSuchMethodError`, and **`directory()` throws** — taking down `agent_directory` and wake-target resolution with it. `FormatException` is caught in `_readRegistry`, but this is a *shape* error, not a parse error, so it escapes.

The sibling method two functions above guards exactly this shape — please mirror it:

```dart
final entry = registry?[id];
final registryCwd = entry is Map<String, dynamic> ? entry['cwd'] : null;
final cwd = (registryCwd is String && registryCwd.isNotEmpty)
    ? registryCwd
    : _decodeSessionCwd?.call(slugDir.name);
```

A regression test with a non-map registry entry (no spawn needed, `MemoryExecutionEnv` suffices) would pin it.

---

### Thread 3 — `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_inbox.dart` line 419

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-21):
💡 **SUGGESTION: the `FileKind.symlink` arm is unreachable on every current backend, and on lstat-semantics backends it re-opens the bug being fixed**

`agent_cli_inbox.dart:419`:

```dart
if (info.isErr || (kind != FileKind.directory && kind != FileKind.symlink)) {
```

Two observations:

1. On the real IO env, `fileInfo` uses `FileStat.stat`, which **follows** symlinks (verified locally: symlink→dir reports `directory`, symlink→file reports `file`), so `FileKind.symlink` is never produced there; `MemoryExecutionEnv` has no symlink model either. The `symlink` arm is dead code today.
2. `FileKind` is documented as pi's semantics: *"Symlinks are not followed automatically."* On any backend honoring that (lstat), **symlink→file** would pass this check and then die with the raw `ProcessException: No such file or directory` — the exact failure mode gh-1744 exists to prevent.

Neither blocks the merge (current hosts behave correctly), but the doc comment's "`Directory(cwd).existsSync()` semantics … symlinks stay allowed" overstates the guarantee. Consider resolving the link (`fileInfo` on the target) or scoping the comment, and note why the arm exists — there is currently no test exercising it (the memory env cannot produce `symlink`).

---

### Thread 4 — `lib/src/session/session_repo.dart` line 174

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-21):
💡 **SUGGESTION: a second, undocumented legacy-slug ambiguity class flips decode**

`session_repo.dart:174` — the reversible marker is "slug contains a recognized `%XX` escape". That detection also catches **legacy on-disk slugs** whose folder names legitimately contained percent-escape-like text. Verified against this diff's decoder:

| legacy on-disk slug | decode before this PR | decode after |
|---|---|---|
| `--tmp-a%2Db--` | `/tmp/a%2Db` | `/tmp/a-b` |
| `--tmp-a%2Fb--` | `/tmp/a%2Fb` | `/tmp/a/b` |
| `--tmp-a%25b--` | `/tmp/a%25b` | `/tmp/a%b` (lossy) |

The PR notes only acknowledge the hyphen ambiguity ("Legacy on-disk slugs of hyphenated projects stay ambiguous (unchanged decode)"); this class is not mentioned. Impact is bounded — the decode only feeds the `directory()` fallback now that the registry's exact cwd is preferred, and a wrong fallback cwd is refused by name in `launchMailboxWake` instead of crashing — so this is documentation, not behavior, work: extend the `decodeSessionCwd` doc comment (and ideally the PR notes) to name the `%2D`/`%2F`/`%5C`/`%3A`/`%25` legacy-text flip.

---

### Thread 5 — `lib/src/session/session_repo.dart` line 122

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-21):
💡 **SUGGESTION: call out the Windows/colon slug churn in the PR notes**

`session_repo.dart:122` — `:` now escapes to `%3A`, so any cwd containing a colon encodes to a **different on-disk slug folder** than the legacy scheme. Unlike hyphens (which occur in maybe some workspace names), a colon is in **every Windows drive-letter path** (`C:\Users\...` → legacy `--C-Users-…--`, new `--C%3A-Users-…--`). Consequence after upgrade: the first new session in each Windows project creates a fresh slug directory — session listing stays correct (cwd comes from file headers, as the PR notes correctly state) but the messaging-fabric root `<root>/<slug>/messages` moves, so old folders coexist and any pending mail in a legacy mailbox directory is left behind until that session is re-registered.

This is the same accepted coexistence trade-off the ticket documents for hyphens, so no code change is requested — one sentence in the PR notes ("every Windows path changes slug; old slug folders coexist") would keep the migration story honest for the Windows hosts this repo builds (`build-windows` legs).

---

# gh-1744: [BUG] Lossy decodeSessionCwd replaces hyphens with slashes breaking mailbox wake for dashed folder names

## Description

## Problem Summary
`decodeSessionCwd` irreversibly turns hyphens in directory names into path separators:
- `lib/src/session/session_repo.dart:109`: `_encodeCwd` replaces `/`, `\`, `:` with `-`.
- `lib/src/session/session_repo.dart:123`: `decodeSessionCwd` does `inner.split('-').join('/')`.

### Impact
For any workspace containing hyphens (e.g., `/Users/Yury_Bakhmutski/_w/postal-nl`), `decodeSessionCwd` decodes it as:
`/Users/Yury_Bakhmutski/_w/postal/nl` (which does not exist!).

Consumers of `decodeSessionCwd`:
1. `file_messaging_repository.dart:373` (`directory()`): populates `MailboxEntry.cwd` with the bogus path.
2. `file_messaging_repository.dart:444` (`_recordRegistry`): persists the non-existent path into `messages-registry.json`.
3. `subagent_tools.dart:624` & `agent_cli.dart:1106` (`_launchMailboxWake`): attempts `Process.start` with `workingDirectory: entry.cwd`, resulting in:
   `ProcessException: No such file or directory`
   The asleep mailbox can never be woken up by incoming agent mail.

## Proposed Fix
1. Encode slug reversibly (e.g. percent-encoding or escaping hyphens as `--`).
2. Have `directory()` and `_launchMailboxWake` prefer the exact verified `cwd` stored in `messages-registry.json` or verify `Directory(cwd).existsSync()` before attempting process spawn.

# gh-1744: [BUG] Lossy decodeSessionCwd replaces hyphens with slashes breaking mailbox wake for dashed folder names

## Description

## Problem Summary
`decodeSessionCwd` irreversibly turns hyphens in directory names into path separators:
- `lib/src/session/session_repo.dart:109`: `_encodeCwd` replaces `/`, `\`, `:` with `-`.
- `lib/src/session/session_repo.dart:123`: `decodeSessionCwd` does `inner.split('-').join('/')`.

### Impact
For any workspace containing hyphens (e.g., `/Users/Yury_Bakhmutski/_w/postal-nl`), `decodeSessionCwd` decodes it as:
`/Users/Yury_Bakhmutski/_w/postal/nl` (which does not exist!).

Consumers of `decodeSessionCwd`:
1. `file_messaging_repository.dart:373` (`directory()`): populates `MailboxEntry.cwd` with the bogus path.
2. `file_messaging_repository.dart:444` (`_recordRegistry`): persists the non-existent path into `messages-registry.json`.
3. `subagent_tools.dart:624` & `agent_cli.dart:1106` (`_launchMailboxWake`): attempts `Process.start` with `workingDirectory: entry.cwd`, resulting in:
   `ProcessException: No such file or directory`
   The asleep mailbox can never be woken up by incoming agent mail.

## Proposed Fix
1. Encode slug reversibly (e.g. percent-encoding or escaping hyphens as `--`).
2. Have `directory()` and `_launchMailboxWake` prefer the exact verified `cwd` stored in `messages-registry.json` or verify `Directory(cwd).existsSync()` before attempting process spawn.

# gh-1744: [BUG] Lossy decodeSessionCwd replaces hyphens with slashes breaking mailbox wake for dashed folder names

## Description

## Problem Summary
`decodeSessionCwd` irreversibly turns hyphens in directory names into path separators:
- `lib/src/session/session_repo.dart:109`: `_encodeCwd` replaces `/`, `\`, `:` with `-`.
- `lib/src/session/session_repo.dart:123`: `decodeSessionCwd` does `inner.split('-').join('/')`.

### Impact
For any workspace containing hyphens (e.g., `/Users/Yury_Bakhmutski/_w/postal-nl`), `decodeSessionCwd` decodes it as:
`/Users/Yury_Bakhmutski/_w/postal/nl` (which does not exist!).

Consumers of `decodeSessionCwd`:
1. `file_messaging_repository.dart:373` (`directory()`): populates `MailboxEntry.cwd` with the bogus path.
2. `file_messaging_repository.dart:444` (`_recordRegistry`): persists the non-existent path into `messages-registry.json`.
3. `subagent_tools.dart:624` & `agent_cli.dart:1106` (`_launchMailboxWake`): attempts `Process.start` with `workingDirectory: entry.cwd`, resulting in:
   `ProcessException: No such file or directory`
   The asleep mailbox can never be woken up by incoming agent mail.

## Proposed Fix
1. Encode slug reversibly (e.g. percent-encoding or escaping hyphens as `--`).
2. Have `directory()` and `_launchMailboxWake` prefer the exact verified `cwd` stored in `messages-registry.json` or verify `Directory(cwd).existsSync()` before attempting process spawn.

- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,

  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >

  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no

This is a structural move; "TDD" here means: run the loc gate first to see it FAIL (RED), move, then see it PASS (GREEN). Also run the moved tests.

2. **Thread 2 (IMPORTANT)** — unguarded registry entry shape in `directory()`. RED: write a regression test with a non-map registry entry (`{"sess1/main": "corupted"}`) expecting `directory()` to not throw and to fall back to slug decode. GREEN: apply the guard `entry is Map<String, dynamic>`.

3. **Thread 3 (SUGESTION)** — symlink arm. Response: scope the doc comment accurately (stat follows symlinks; symlink arm is a defensive allowance for lstat-semantics backends; symlink→file on such a backend would re-open the bug — acknowledge), and add a test exercising the symlink arm with a stub env that reports `FileKind.symlink` for an existing directory path. The reviewer explicitly noted "there is currently no test exercising it (the memory env cannot produce symlink)". A stub env can. Also scope the doc comment to not overstate: change "(`Directory(cwd).existsSync()` semantics: existing and not a plain file; symlinks stay allowed)" to something accurate.

  Should I also make the code resolve the link? The reviewer says "Consider resolving the link (fileInfo on the target) or scoping the comment, and note why the arm exists". Both acceptable; the minimal, no-behavior-change option is scoping the comment + adding the test. I'll do that: doc comment + a stub-env test pining the symlink arm behavior (a symlink-kind entry that names an existing dir → spawn proceeds).

  Wait — what should the behavior of the arm be in the test? On a stat-following backend, `fileInfo(symlink)` returns target's kind, so symlink kind never appears. On an lstat backend, symlink→dir reports symlink → exec proceeds (exec with cwd through symlink works, kernel follows). Symlink→file on lstat reports symlink too (pi semantics: not followed) → passes the check → exec fails with raw ProcessException. Hmm, that's the bug re-open scenario. Should the code be hardened against that? The reviewer explicitly says "Neither blocks the merge (current hosts behave correctly)... Consider resolving the link (fileInfo on the target) or scoping the comment".

  Option A: resolve the link — when kind == symlink, `fileInfo` on the target to check it's a directory. But `ExecutionEnv` API has no readLink; resolving "the target" from a path isn't possible generically. We could just refuse symlinks... no — on stat backends symlink→dir reports `directory` anyway; the symlink arm only matters on lstat backends. If we dropped the symlink arm, lstat backends would refuse symlink→dir (a false refusal, but a refusal names the path, safe-ish). Honestly the cleanest hardening that keeps stat-backend behavior unchanged AND fixes the lstat→file hole: only allow `directory` kind... but then on lstat backends symlink→dir wakes fail with refusal (named, not crashing) — acceptable and safer. But that changes semantics the PR deliberately wrote (with the comment "symlinks stay allowed").

  The reviewer gave explicit permission to keep behavior and just scope the comment + note why the arm exists + ideally exercise the arm in a test. I'll go minimal: fix the doc comment, keep the arm, add the stub test. That matches "this is documentation, not behavior, work" spirit for suggestions.

- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files

Response: scope the doc comment accurately (stat follows symlinks; symlink arm is a defensive allowance for lstat-semantics backends; symlink→file on such a backend would re-open the bug — acknowledge), and add a test exercising the symlink arm with a stub env that reports `FileKind.symlink` for an existing directory path. The reviewer explicitly noted "there is currently no test exercising it (the memory env cannot produce symlink)". A stub env can. Also scope the doc comment to not overstate: change "(`Directory(cwd).existsSync()` semantics: existing and not a plain file; symlinks stay allowed)" to something accurate.

  Should I also make the code resolve the link? The reviewer says "Consider resolving the link (fileInfo on the target) or scoping the comment, and note why the arm exists". Both acceptable; the minimal, no-behavior-change option is scoping the comment + adding the test. I'll do that: doc comment + a stub-env test pining the symlink arm behavior (a symlink-kind entry that names an existing dir → spawn proceeds).

  Wait — what should the behavior of the arm be in the test? On a stat-following backend, `fileInfo(symlink)` returns target's kind, so symlink kind never appears. On an lstat backend, symlink→dir reports symlink → exec proceeds (exec with cwd through symlink works, kernel follows). Symlink→file on lstat reports symlink too (pi semantics: not followed) → passes the check → exec fails with raw ProcessException. Hmm, that's the bug re-open scenario. Should the code be hardened against that? The reviewer explicitly says "Neither blocks the merge (current hosts behave correctly)... Consider resolving the link (fileInfo on the target) or scoping the comment".

  Option A: resolve the link — when kind == symlink, `fileInfo` on the target to check it's a directory. But `ExecutionEnv` API has no readLink; resolving "the target" from a path isn't possible generically. We could just refuse symlinks... no — on stat backends symlink→dir reports `directory` anyway; the symlink arm only matters on lstat backends. If we dropped the symlink arm, lstat backends would refuse symlink→dir (a false refusal, but a refusal names the path, safe-ish). Honestly the cleanest hardening that keeps stat-backend behavior unchanged AND fixes the lstat→file hole: only allow `directory` kind... but then on lstat backends symlink→dir wakes fail with refusal (named, not crashing) — acceptable and safer. But that changes semantics the PR deliberately wrote (with the comment "symlinks stay allowed").

  The reviewer gave explicit permission to keep behavior and just scope the comment + note why the arm exists + ideally exercise the arm in a test. I'll go minimal: fix the doc comment, keep the arm, add the stub test. That matches "this is documentation, not behavior, work" spirit for suggestions.

It uses `FileStat.stat` — which FOLOWS symlinks. `FileStat.stat` on a symlink returns the target's type: `FileSystemEntityType.file` or `.directory`. `FileSystemEntityType.link` only comes from `lstat` (`FileSystemEntity.typeSync(path, followLinks: false)`). Since `FileStat.stat` follows links, `stat.type` can never be `.link`... Actually, is that true? Dart docs: `FileStat.stat` — "Asynchronously calls `FileSystemEntity.stat()`... If path is a symbolic link, the link is followed and the result describes the target." So `.link` from `FileStat.stat` is unreachable — consistent with the reviewer's verification ("symlink→dir reports directory, symlink→file reports file; FileKind.symlink is never produced there"). FileStat.stat on a broken symlink returns stat with type... on Linux, stat on a broken link fails with ENOENT → FileStat with type notFound. So no link type). Interesting — this is the `fileInfo` in `io_execution_env.dart` (line ~235-260). It uses `FileStat.stat` — which FOLOWS symlinks. `FileStat.stat` on a symlink returns the target's type: `FileSystemEntityType.file` or `.directory`. `FileSystemEntityType.link` only comes from `lstat` (`FileSystemEntity.typeSync(path, followLinks: false)`). Since `FileStat.stat` follows links, `stat.type` can never be `.link`... Actually, is that true? Dart docs: `FileStat.stat` — "Asynchronously calls `FileSystemEntity.stat()`... If path is a symbolic link, the link is followed and the result describes the target." So `.link` from `FileStat.stat` is unreachable — consistent with the reviewer's verification ("symlink→dir reports directory, symlink→file reports file; FileKind.symlink is never produced there"). So the `FileSystemEntityType.link => FileKind.symlink` arm in io env is itself dead code via stat — but it maps to FileKind.symlink only if stat ever returned link, which it doesn't (except maybe broken links? FileStat.stat on a broken symlink returns stat with type... on Linux, stat on a broken link fails with ENOENT → FileStat with type notFound. So no link type). The reviewer's claim holds: no current backend produces `FileKind.symlink` from `fileInfo`.

If path is a symbolic link, the link is followed and the result describes the target." So `.link` from `FileStat.stat` is unreachable — consistent with the reviewer's verification ("symlink→dir reports directory, symlink→file reports file; FileKind.symlink is never produced there"). Since `FileStat.stat` follows links, `stat.type` can never be `.link`... Actually, is that true? Dart docs: `FileStat.stat` — "Asynchronously calls `FileSystemEntity.stat()`... If path is a symbolic link, the link is followed and the result describes the target." So `.link` from `FileStat.stat` is unreachable — consistent with the reviewer's verification ("symlink→dir reports directory, symlink→file reports file; FileKind.symlink is never produced there"). FileStat.stat on a broken symlink returns stat with type... on Linux, stat on a broken link fails with ENOENT → FileStat with type notFound. So no link type). Interesting — this is the `fileInfo` in `io_execution_env.dart` (line ~235-260). It uses `FileStat.stat` — which FOLOWS symlinks. `FileStat.stat` on a symlink returns the target's type: `FileSystemEntityType.file` or `.directory`. `FileSystemEntityType.link` only comes from `lstat` (`FileSystemEntity.typeSync(path, followLinks: false)`). Since `FileStat.stat` follows links, `stat.type` can never be `.link`... Actually, is that true? Dart docs: `FileStat.stat` — "Asynchronously calls `FileSystemEntity.stat()`... If path is a symbolic link, the link is followed and the result describes the target." So `.link` from `FileStat.stat` is unreachable — consistent with the reviewer's verification ("symlink→dir reports directory, symlink→file reports file; FileKind.symlink is never produced there"). So the `FileSystemEntityType.link => FileKind.symlink` arm in io env is itself dead code via stat — but it maps to FileKind.symlink only if stat ever returned link, which it doesn't (except maybe broken links? FileStat.stat on a broken symlink returns stat with type... on Linux, stat on a broken link fails with ENOENT → FileStat with type notFound. So no link type). The reviewer's claim holds: no current backend produces `FileKind.symlink` from `fileInfo`.

Interesting — this is the `fileInfo` in `io_execution_env.dart` (line ~235-260). It uses `FileStat.stat` — which FOLOWS symlinks. `FileStat.stat` on a symlink returns the target's type: `FileSystemEntityType.file` or `.directory`. `FileSystemEntityType.link` only comes from `lstat` (`FileSystemEntity.typeSync(path, followLinks: false)`). Since `FileStat.stat` follows links, `stat.type` can never be `.link`... Actually, is that true? Dart docs: `FileStat.stat` — "Asynchronously calls `FileSystemEntity.stat()`... If path is a symbolic link, the link is followed and the result describes the target." So `.link` from `FileStat.stat` is unreachable — consistent with the reviewer's verification ("symlink→dir reports directory, symlink→file reports file; FileKind.symlink is never produced there"). So the `FileSystemEntityType.link => FileKind.symlink` arm in io env is itself dead code via stat — but it maps to FileKind.symlink only if stat ever returned link, which it doesn't (except maybe broken links? FileStat.stat on a broken symlink returns stat with type... on Linux, stat on a broken link fails with ENOENT → FileStat with type notFound. So no link type). The reviewer's claim holds: no current backend produces `FileKind.symlink` from `fileInfo`.

Since `FileStat.stat` follows links, `stat.type` can never be `.link`... Actually, is that true? Dart docs: `FileStat.stat` — "Asynchronously calls `FileSystemEntity.stat()`... If path is a symbolic link, the link is followed and the result describes the target." So `.link` from `FileStat.stat` is unreachable — consistent with the reviewer's verification ("symlink→dir reports directory, symlink→file reports file; FileKind.symlink is never produced there"). FileStat.stat on a broken symlink returns stat with type... on Linux, stat on a broken link fails with ENOENT → FileStat with type notFound. So no link type). {"content":"## 💡 Thread: `FileKind.symlink` arm unreachable / doc overstates the guarantee — **comment scoped + arm now test-pinned**

Took the documentation path (no behavior change — agreed the current hosts behave correctly):

- The `launchMailboxWake` doc comment no longer claims `Directory(cwd).existsSync()` "symlinks stay allowed" semantics. It now states precisely what is guaranteed: **backend kind semantics, not link resolution** — the real IO env stats *through* symlinks (`FileStat.stat`, so link→directory reports `FileKind.directory` and symlinked workspaces wake), `MemoryExecutionEnv` has no symlink model, therefore no current backend produces `FileKind.symlink` here.
- It also documents **why the arm exists**: defensive, for a hypothetical backend honoring pi's lstat contract ("symlinks are not followed automatically") where a symlink-kind path naming an existing directory must still wake — the spawn itself follows the link. And it names the accepted hole you flagged: on such a backend a link to a plain *file* also passes the check and fails at the spawn (accepted while no backend reports the kind).
- The arm is no longer untested: `test/cli/agent_cli_mailbox_wake_test.dart` adds `spawns for a symlink-kind cwd (lstat-semantics backends)`, using a `_SymlinkCwdEnv` stub whose `fileInfo` reports `FileKind.symlink` (pi semantics) for an existing directory — pins that the guard allows the spawn. Took the documentation path (no behavior change — agreed the current hosts behave correctly):

- The `launchMailboxWake` doc comment no longer claims `Directory(cwd).existsSync()` "symlinks stay allowed" semantics. It now states precisely what is guaranteed: **backend kind semantics, not link resolution** — the real IO env stats *through* symlinks (`FileStat.stat`, so link→directory reports `FileKind.directory` and symlinked workspaces wake), `MemoryExecutionEnv` has no symlink model, therefore no current backend produces `FileKind.symlink` here.
- It also documents **why the arm exists**: defensive, for a hypothetical backend honoring pi's lstat contract ("symlinks are not followed automatically") where a symlink-kind path naming an existing directory must still wake — the spawn itself follows the link. blocks.text:
No `set-exit-if-changed` in ci.yml — CI does NOT enforce dart format (only the pre-commit hook self-heals staged files locally). So:

- The tree at HEAD is old-style formatted (formatted with an older dart, e.g. 3.6.x tall-style-off era or before tall style). 
- CI has no format gate. The `static` leg runs `dart analyze` presumably.
- Therefore: I must NOT run whole-file `dart format` on files whose style is old-style — it produces unrelated churn. 

BUT my new code must still LOOK consistent. What style should my new code be? The pre-commit hook would reformat staged files with the local dart (3.13.5 tall style) when I commit... wait, that would reformat the ENTIRE staged file including pre-existing old-style parts — meaning committing via the hook would produce exactly the churn I'm trying to avoid, and apparently that's how the repo works?? But then main would be tall-style everywhere... unless commits are made with --no-verify or the contributors' dart is older.

Let me check what dart version produced main's style. The `.any((m) => const {...}.contains(...))` style with that specific indentation (continuation aligned under `.any(`) is the OLD (pre-3.7) dart format style. Dart 3.7 introduced the tall style by default. main's files are old-style → main was last formatted with dart < 3.7. But this sandbox has dart 3.13.5. +/// is "the slug carries a recognized `%XX` escape", so a legacy folder
+/// whose name legitimately contained escape-like TEXT flips its decode —
+/// `%2D`, `%2F`, `%5C`, `%3A` and `%25` present in legacy slug text now
+/// unescape (e.g. `--tmp-a%2Fb--` decoded literally before this change,
+/// and decodes to `/tmp/a/b` now; `--tmp-a%2Db--` → `/tmp/a-b`;
+/// `--tmp-a%25b--` → `/tmp/a%b`). Impact is bounded: the decode only
+/// feeds the messaging `directory()` cwd fallback — the registry's exact
+/// cwd is preferred — and a wrong fallback cwd is refused by name in

# PR #1751 rework — gh-1744 review rework

All 5 open review threads addressed: the BLOCKING CI/loc-gate failure fixed, the IMPORTANT registry-shape crash fixed with regression tests (TDD: RED → GREEN), and the 3 suggestions resolved at the documentation/test level. Full suite green on the rework head.

## Issues/Notes

- **BLOCKING (thread `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6u4FSr`)** — `test/cli/agent_cli_test.dart` was 2861 lines, over the 2800-line god-file ceiling (`guards` loc leg + aggregate `Quality gate` red). **fixed** (see Approach).
- **IMPORTANT (thread `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6u4FWb`)** — `directory()` read `registry?[id]?['cwd']` unguarded: a valid-JSON registry with a non-map entry threw an uncaught `NoSuchMethodError` and killed the whole mailbox listing. **fixed**, plus the same shape-error class one level up: `_readRegistry`/`_recordRegistry` used `jsonDecode(...) as Map<String, dynamic>`, whose `TypeError` for a non-map top-level document also escapes `on FormatException`.
- **SUGGESTION (thread `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6u4FZ3`)** — `FileKind.symlink` arm unreachable on current backends, doc comment overstated the guarantee, no test exercised the arm. **addressed**: comment scoped to accurate backend kind semantics + the arm is now pinned by a stub-based test.
- **SUGGESTION (thread `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6u4FcQ`)** — undocumented second legacy-slug ambiguity class (escape-like text `%2D`/`%2F`/`%5C`/`%3A`/`%25` in legacy slug names flips decode). **addressed**: `decodeSessionCwd` doc comment extended; PR notes updated.
- **SUGGESTION (thread `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6u4FgE`)** — Windows/colon slug churn missing from the PR notes. **addressed**: sentence added to the PR description's Notes section.
- Owned CI violations: none open — the rework head's only red (the loc gate, the BLOCKING thread) is fixed; `ci_failures.md` reports no failed checks at rework start. Local parity re-runs: loc gate PASS (944 files within limits, exit 0), `crap4dart check --baseline` PASS (loc + CRAP ratchet ≤90 + duplication, exit 0), `dart analyze` clean.

## Approach

1. **God-file ceiling (TDD: RED → GREEN)** — RED reproduced locally: `crap4dart check --config crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml --only loc` → `[FAIL] test/cli/agent_cli_test.dart: 2861 lines > max 2800`, exit 2. GREEN: moved the wake concern out per the reviewer's option 1 — `group('mailboxWakeCommand')` + `group('launchMailboxWake')` + `_RecordingShell` now live in the new `test/cli/agent_cli_mailbox_wake_test.dart` (public API only, no `part` gymnastics; the reviewer's suggested name `agent_cli_inbox_wake_test.dart` is taken by the gh-1180 wake-lane suite). `agent_cli_test.dart`: 2861 → **2767 lines**; gate re-run → `[PASS] loc: 944 files within 944 limits`, exit 0.
2. **Registry shape guard (TDD: RED → GREEN)** — RED: 3 new regression tests in `file_messaging_repository_test.dart` failed exactly as predicted (`String is not a subtype of int of 'index'` at `directory()`; `List<dynamic> is not a subtype of Map<String, dynamic>` in `_readRegistry`; corrupt doc preserved by `register`). GREEN: `directory()` mirrors the reviewer's snippet (`entry is Map<String, dynamic>` guard, slug-decode fallback); `_readRegistry` returns `null` for a non-map document; `_recordRegistry` starts fresh instead of preserving/rethrowing.
3. **Symlink arm** — no behavior change (agreed: current hosts are correct). `launchMailboxWake`'s doc comment now states what is guaranteed (backend kind semantics — real IO stats *through* symlinks, memory env has no symlink model) and why the defensive arm exists (pi lstat-semantics backends), including the accepted symlink→file hole; new test `spawns for a symlink-kind cwd (lstat-semantics backends)` pins the arm via a `_SymlinkCwdEnv` stub.
4. **Docs** — `decodeSessionCwd` doc comment names the legacy escape-text flip class and why its impact is bounded (registry-preferred cwd + named refusal in `launchMailboxWake`); PR description Notes extended with the Windows `:`→`%3A` slug-churn sentence (via `gh pr edit`).

## Files Modified

- `test/cli/agent_cli_mailbox_wake_test.dart` — **new**: moved `mailboxWakeCommand` + `launchMailboxWake` groups and `_RecordingShell`, plus the new symlink-kind test and its `_SymlinkCwdEnv` stub.

- `lib/src/messaging/file_messaging_repository.dart` — shape guards in `directory()`, `_readRegistry()`, `_recordRegistry()`.
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_inbox.dart` — `launchMailboxWake` doc comment scoped (symlink semantics + rationale).
- `lib/src/session/session_repo.dart` — `decodeSessionCwd` doc comment extended (second legacy ambiguity class).
- `test/messaging/file_messaging_repository_test.dart` — 3 regression tests for the registry shape guards.
- PR description (`gh pr edit 1751`) — Windows/colon slug churn + legacy escape-text class added to Notes.

## Test Coverage
